samples.summary: scoreAll's headline claim — a mixed-panel pass is REFUSED before the API budget is spent — has no test
samples.evidence: `scoreAll` gains two new pre-budget guards (score-all.mjs:721-724): the `--panel-digest must be sha256:<64 hex>` refusal and the `resolvePanelDigest(...)` refusal when the replicates' envelopes state two panels. The USAGE text and the block comment sell this as the point of the change ("replicates whose recorded panel_digest disagrees are refused before the budget is spent"). score-all.test.mjs has no test for either: grepping the whole file for `mixed`/`MIXED` (lines 219, 261-285, 695-706 only) finds only `persistArgs`/`renderArgs` flag-shape assertions and the fullPassSpy fixture; no `assert.rejects` for a mixed store and none for a malformed `--panel-digest`. The existing `assert.rejects` cases (lines 619-646, 798) cover only root/corpus/run-id pre-checks. The one pass-level assertion of the new field (line 1096) is `result.panel_digest === PANEL_DIGEST_ABSENT`, i.e. a store where NO replicate records a digest — so neither the real-digest happy path nor the mixed path nor `allowMixedPanel` is exercised end to end. A guard that never refuses in any test is a guard whose removal is invisible.

samples.summary: report.mjs's new `resolvePanel` (the CLI's whole panel-resolution rule, incl. the stated→`reconstructed` mapping and exit 2) is unreachable by any test, and score-all's fixture re-implements it instead
samples.evidence: `resolvePanel` is a closure inside `main()` in report.mjs (added ~3358-3389): it validates `--panel-digest` and `process.exit(2)`s on a bad one, stamps `source: "reconstructed"` for a stated digest, warns on `mixed`, and warns on `not-recorded`. report.test.mjs contains no CLI/main test at all — grep for `resolvePanel`, `--panel-digest`, `not-recorded`, `PANEL_DIGEST_ABSENT` in report.test.mjs returns no matches. The change's own docblock above `withPanelStamp` states the principle it then violates: "stamping written inside the CLI could not be reached by any test, and replacing `panel.source` with a hardcoded `"files"` … survived undetected" — yet the source-selection logic itself stayed in the CLI. Worse, the only place this rule is exercised is score-all.test.mjs:694-701, where the spy HAND-REIMPLEMENTS it (`const source = stated ? "reconstructed" : resolved?.source`), so the fixture would keep passing if report.mjs's real rule regressed to `files` or to the wrong runId branch. Same applies to the new `runId: args.scope === "per-run" ? runIds[0] : null` change at report.mjs:3420, which nothing in report.test.mjs covers.

samples.summary: The new `listRuns({ panelDigest })` filter has no test
samples.evidence: store.mjs:1105/1119 adds a `panelDigest` filter to `listRuns`, documented as "the one a cross-run scorer wants". store.test.mjs's `listRuns` test (lines 775-810) asserts `configHash`, `corpusVersion` and `panelSha` filters (including the negative case `listRuns({ panelSha: "f".repeat(40) }) === []`) but never passes `panelDigest`. Deleting the new `if (panelDigest && ...) continue;` line would leave the whole suite green; no other file calls `listRuns` with it (grep across scripts/agent).

samples.summary: The backfill CLI `main()` in panel-identity.mjs is unexported and untested — including the `--at <ref>` git read and the `--allow-absent` absent-file report
samples.evidence: panel-identity.mjs:505-542 implements flag parsing (`--at`, `--prefix`, `--dir`, `--allow-absent`, `--help`), the `git show <ref>:<prefix><rel>` reader, and the stderr report naming absent files. `main` is not exported and panel-identity.test.mjs imports only the pure helpers (lines 19-34); no test spawns the script either (no `execFileSync`/child_process in panel-identity.test.mjs). This is the tool the change relies on for reconstructing pilot digests, and its argument handling (e.g. `flag("at")` returning the next argv element, prefix defaulting) is exactly the kind of code that breaks silently. Extracting `main` or a `panelDigestAt({at, prefix, exec})` seam would make it reachable, mirroring the `withPanelStamp` extraction done in report.mjs for the same stated reason.

samples.summary: The "no DEAD entries in NOT_PANEL_FILES" assertion does not test deadness — it only checks the file exists on disk, and its first conjunct is always true
samples.evidence: panel-identity.test.mjs:87-91 comments "the register holds no DEAD entries. An exclusion for a module nothing imports any more is a reason nobody will re-read", but asserts `seen.size > 0 && existsSync(path.join(AGENT_DIR, file))`. `seen` always contains `PANEL_ENTRY`, so `seen.size > 0` is a constant true; and `existsSync` passes for any module still present in scripts/agent regardless of whether anything reachable from the panel imports it. A `NOT_PANEL_FILES` entry for a module the panel no longer imports at all — precisely the stale entry the comment describes — passes this assertion. Testing the claim needs the set of specifiers actually collected during the walk (which the test already has) rather than the filesystem.

samples.summary: run.mjs stamps `panel_digest_source` and `panel_digest_version` into run.json and every item envelope; no test asserts either landed
samples.evidence: run.mjs:881-889 and :998-1000 add `panel_digest`, `panel_digest_source` and `panel_digest_version` to run.json and each item envelope. run.test.mjs asserts the analogous commit fields off the STORE (lines 982-984: `got.envelope.panel_sha`, `got.envelope.panel_sha_source === "flag"`; line 1004 `run.runJson.panel_sha`) but grepping run.test.mjs for `panel_digest` finds only `resolvePanelDigest` unit assertions (563-587) and the `--panel-digest` argv at line 271 — nothing reads the stored envelope's or run.json's digest fields. `panel_digest` itself is indirectly forced by `validateRunEnvelope`, but dropping `panel_digest_source`/`panel_digest_version` from the stamp (or writing the wrong source, e.g. `"files"` for a flag-stated run) would leave the suite green, and `validateScorePanel` downstream depends on that vocabulary being right.

samples.summary: `assert.equal(digest, panelDigestOf(AGENT_DIR))` is a determinism check over a pure function and cannot fail
samples.evidence: panel-identity.test.mjs:180-182 calls `panelDigestOf(AGENT_DIR)` twice and asserts equality, described as "the digest is stable across two calls". `panelDigestOf` is a pure read + sha256 with no cache, ordering or clock input, so the assertion holds for any implementation that does not read a random source; it carries no information beyond the `isPanelDigest` check on the line above. Harmless, but it is presented as one of the three properties this test establishes.

verdict.reason: The two pre-budget panel guards in scoreAll (score-all.mjs:721-723 malformed --panel-digest refusal; :724 resolvePanelDigest mixed refusal, both above assertBudget at :737) have no test that exercises them. scoreAll is imported only by score-all.test.mjs (repo-wide grep for `scoreAll` finds no other caller, no CLI-subprocess test, nothing in .github or other *.test.mjs). In that file every assert.rejects (619, 623, 636, 644-646, 798) covers replicate-count, duplicate-replicate, root/corpus/config-hash and the corpus-directory message; no call passes a malformed panelDigest, and store.putRun is used only twice (742, 1065) with `{ runJson: { run_id } }`, so neither end-to-end pass has replicates recording any digest — hence the only pass-level assertion is result.panel_digest === PANEL_DIGEST_ABSENT (1096). The panelDigest/allowMixedPanel mentions at 220-221 and 268-285 are argv-shape assertions on panelFlags/persistArgs/renderArgs, and 695/706 are the child-emulating fixture, not the driver's guard. The closest coverage is helper-level in panel-identity.test.mjs (238-245 mixed refusal, 248-252 allowMixed, 265-267 malformed) — real, but it bypasses scoreAll entirely: removing score-all.mjs:721-723 or forcing allowMixed:true at :724 breaks no test. So the headline behavior ("replicates whose recorded panel_digest disagrees are refused before the budget is spent", USAGE :868-870) ships without a meaningful test — a major missing-test finding under this lens.
